dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: #We meet again at last, {NICKNAME}. How have things been with you lately?

choices.text: Thanks for asking! How's it been for you in Fontaine?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Honestly? Some good and some bad. Let's get the bad out of the way first...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: As I was crossing some open water on my Soulsniper, I drifted a bit too close to the shooting range. The Special Patrol mistook me for an airborne target and let off two volleys in my direction...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Luckily, I was moving fast enough that they couldn't lead the shots properly. Not a single round connected, and Captain Chevreuse arrived in time to call a halt to things.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Well, only good things followed after that...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I took a few easy turns through the city, taking my time to admire all the exquisite man-made architecture, the elaborate machines and ornaments, and the beautifully intricate clothes.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I'd been a little worried beforehand. The Court of Fontaine is a fortress walled in by stone — I wondered whether the limited sightlines might feel oppressive.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: As it turned out, the experience was just the opposite of life in the Flower-Feather Clan. Being surrounded by towering buildings gave me, somehow, a strange and pleasant sense of safety.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Once the wargame's over, I'd like to take a couple more turns through the city.

choices.text: As long as there were no misunderstandings or friction...
First, what's it been like working with the Special Patrol?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Well above expectations — and not just by a little bit.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Their discipline is remarkable. Although I can already imagine some of the tribal warriors finding them too rigid, too tied up by rules to fight freely...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...But after training new recruits whose baseline skills were all over the map, I gradually came to understand.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: When individuals don't have overwhelming personal strength, cooperation and discipline are the last guarantee of stable combat power.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: So I've had a thought — though it might not be one I can act on—

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Bringing Captain Chevreuse back to Natlan with me, and getting her to throw in with the Flower-Feather Clan's warriors.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: The Mora question would be tricky, naturally. Fontaine's wages and cost-of-living are both on the higher end... but I'd find a way to put together an offer she'd be happy with — beyond just Mora.

choices.text: You think the Special Patrol is stronger than the Saurian-riders?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: No, this isn't about who's stronger or weaker. The point is to make up for what we lack with what they have.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I'm proud of the Flower-Feather Clan's warriors, and I've never doubted the Saurian-riders' ability to take down any monster.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: But it's precisely because I know and trust them that I'm clear on our weak spots. In every battle, we inevitably take a certain amount of casualties.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: In the past, we've held together as tribes — each warrior doing their part in battle, our coordination looking decent enough on the surface.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: But when it comes to bringing together the processes of "responding to losses," "training efficiently," and "replenishing combat strength" — making warrior teams more resilient...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Our friends in Fontaine clearly have a wealth of experience worth studying in depth, so we can grow stronger ourselves.

choices.text: I think I see what you mean...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Managing teams, designing training programs, giving precise commands... in these areas, Captain Chevreuse must be one of Fontaine's foremost experts, no?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Her professional skills, to a warrior pursuing collective strength, are like... a slab of meat sizzling on the open coals to a starving soul.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She really is essential to Fontaine.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You could absolutely call her one of its key figures.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Mm... a shame, then. Fontaine certainly won't let her go.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Poaching from an allied force isn't exactly something a proper warrior of the tribe should be doing.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Just take it as a not-so-appropriate joke on my part.

choices.text: Not quite following — please go on...
I figured you'd consider the warriors stronger.
All good — I'll catch up with you again later.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Same as ever, then. Always run off your feet.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: As for the candidates we'll send to Fontaine for the long-term exchange...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: My top picks are Zhunan and Inkanak. The two of them coming together should work out quite well.
